A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same ProPINN research. The complete main texts and appendices support matching the methods, proofs, experiments, tables and figures despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original ProPINN evaluations on six PDE tasks, component ablations, scalability studies and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds training diagnostics and controlled experiments in Appendices A, B and F.

M1.justification: The proposed differential perturbation, shared projection, regional pooling, multi-region MLP mixing and output head remain unchanged in Equations (6)-(7). The additional optimizer combinations and regularization comparator are evaluation variants of the retained architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Convection, 1D-Reaction, Allen-Cahn, 1D-Wave, Karman Vortex and Fluid Dynamics. V2's additional analyses use these existing tasks without extending the represented domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds ProPINN combined with RoPINN to the integration comparison in Figure 7(b), and vanilla PINN with gradient-correlation regularization to Table 7. The seven baseline architectures in the principal benchmark comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces substantial additional evaluation controls: 2,000/4,000-iteration training and a deeper PINN for efficiency comparisons, plus 100 Adam iterations followed by 1,000 L-BFGS iterations across four benchmarks (Appendix F, Tables 5-6). These are additional protocols; the original benchmark settings remain.

E4.justification: New analyses examine gradient-correlation maps on the other three standard benchmarks, correlation/loss/error trajectories during training, additional computation budgets, optimizer choice and direct correlation regularization. RoPINN integration also extends the existing integration study. The original component ablations, scalability and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times. V1 Appendix E/Table 5 and v2 Appendix H/Table 8 report identical standard deviations and p-values, with no changed uncertainty-estimation practice documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial diagnostic and controlled-experiment results in Figures 7(b), 8-9 and Tables 5-7. Its 0.008 Convection rMAE at 2,000/4,000 iterations is a new longer-budget result. Main-table ProPINN scores are unchanged. SetPINN rRMSE changes from 0.031/0.046/0.332 to 0.033/0.034/0.353 for Convection/Reaction/Wave, and from 0.218 to 0.209 for Karman Vortex.

T1.justification: Definition 3.4 replaces the finite-step output difference with a step-normalized infinitesimal limit. Accordingly, the proof changes from an approximate proportionality to exact equality with gradient correlation. Assumption 3.7 now constrains signed inner products, replacing nonnegativity of an already nonnegative norm. The gradient-improvement proof and local-radius derivation are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion drop the claim to the 'first' formal study, modestly narrowing their priority claim, although priority language remains elsewhere. The central gradient-correlation explanation, architecture contribution and 46% headline improvement are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds a tentative explanation of declining correlations through independent local overfitting, and discusses why longer training or direct correlation regularization may not resolve propagation failure. It also identifies convergence and optimizer analysis as future work. The existing high-dimensional PDE limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses a single A100 40GB GPU, Adam with learning rate 0.001 for the retained Fluid Dynamics experiment, and additional baseline-result provenance information. It also documents interlaced point sets and a 0.001 regularization weight for the new comparator. These disclosures do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Jacot et al. neural tangent kernel and Kingma–Ba Adam references, and removes the Langley paper-writing reference. RoPINN, already cited in v1, is now explicitly evaluated and positioned as complementary to ProPINN. The broader related-work framing remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes copyedits and explanatory refinements, changes the order of visualization and efficiency discussion, reorganizes the appendices and adds a Broader Impacts section. The main section sequence and much of the existing narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and rearrangement of displays. V1 Figure 6 is incorporated into v2 Table 1, and v1 Figures 8-9 are combined into v2 Figure 7. New diagnostic Figures 8-9 and experimental Tables 5-7 accompany these presentation changes.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through training diagnostics and controls for computation budget, optimizer choice and direct regularization. The normalized propagation definition and signed-gradient assumption improve mathematical precision. However, Appendix C.4 removes absolute values from the radius denominator without establishing its positivity, leaving a theoretical gap. The added evidence and clarification support a limited net improvement despite this issue.
